summary: This file defines a Player class that holds one soccer player's name, position, and number of goals scored. It is a data-carrying class: later exercises build a list of Player objects and run stream pipelines over them to group and rank the players.

lines.text: Declares the Player class, the blueprint every individual player object will be built from.
Stores the player's name. Marking the field private keeps it out of reach of other classes, and final means it can never change once the object is built.
Holds the position the player plays, such as Forward or Goalkeeper. Stream pipelines will group players by this value.
Holds the goals scored as a whole number, which is what the top-scorer pipelines will compare.

lines.code: public Player(String name, String position, int goals) {
lines.text: The constructor takes all three pieces of information at once, so a Player can never exist in a half-filled state.
Copies the constructor's name argument into the object's own field; this.name distinguishes the field from the parameter of the same name.
A getter gives read-only access to the private name. Streams need these methods to pull values out of each player.
Supplies the position to grouping pipelines, which call it through a method reference like Player::getPosition.
Supplies the goal count for comparisons, used by pipelines that search for the highest scorer.
Tells the compiler that the method below is deliberately replacing a method inherited from Object, so a typo in the name becomes an error instead of a silent bug.
Defines how a Player appears when printed. Without it, printing a player shows a meaningless memory reference instead of readable data.
Begins assembling the readable description; the following lines concatenate each field onto the end of this string.
Wraps the name in single quotes. The escape sequence '\'' is how you write a single-quote character in Java source.
